title: Sex life: Am I in my prime?
gist: Prompted by 'The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie,' sex worker and author Tilly Lawless argues that both 'regretful parent' narratives and pro-natalist 'children give life meaning' narratives over-determine parenthood's role in self-worth, and contends declining birth rates are only a real problem if one also opposes immigration as an offsetting solution.

insights.claim: The author argues that both the 'Regretful Parents' online narrative (parents lamenting a stolen 'prime') and the mainstream 'children give one's life meaning' narrative are two sides of the same over-determined cultural framing, and that neither needs to define a person's sense of being in their prime.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: A reusable framing for reading any cultural debate about parenthood and fulfillment: look for the unstated assumption that children must be either the source or the theft of life's meaning, when both framings can be simultaneously true or false.
insights.quote: I see this same sentiment coursing through the 'Regretful Parents' subreddit today, where parents lament their stolen prime, in direct opposition to the widely promulgated idea that children give one's life meaning.
insights.locator: Notably, Miss Brodie herself also has sexual intercourse

insights.claim: Actor Seth Rogen faced public backlash, including fellow actor Timothée Chalamet calling his stance 'bleak,' for being married and openly happy about being childless — evidence of strong social stigma specifically against voluntary childlessness.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: A concrete, named data point on how celebrity culture still penalizes public statements of contentment with childlessness, useful context for reading demographic/culture commentary on falling birth rates.
insights.locator: I think of American actor Seth Rogen's comments

insights.claim: The author contends that a declining birth rate is only a genuine societal problem for those who also oppose immigration as a way to support aging populations — otherwise, given current global population levels, there is no shortage of people.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Reframes the 'demographic crisis' narrative used to justify pro-natalist policy as implicitly bundled with anti-immigration politics — worth noting when evaluating pro-natalist policy arguments for what they assume about immigration.
insights.quote: The declining birth rate is only an issue if you're anti-immigration; otherwise we have more than enough people to support older generations.
insights.locator: Isn't the world overpopulated as it is?

insights.claim: The author distinguishes healthy parenthood from cases where a parent 'merges their own identity' with a child's achievements to live vicariously through them, citing stage parents like Kit Culkin and the mother figure in Alberto Moravia's 'The Woman of Rome' as examples of parenthood that extracts value from a child rather than adding it.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: A useful lens for distinguishing exploitative versus healthy parent-child dynamics in celebrity and cultural commentary, beyond the simple pro/anti-natalist binary.
insights.quote: She has for her daughter 'the kind of love the housewife feels for a laying hen'.
insights.locator: Stage parents such as Kit Culkin
